# Standard operating procedure

How the team flies a slot. The checklists (`checklists.md`) are the lines read aloud; the emergency procedures (`emergency_procedures.md`) are what happens when a flight goes wrong.

## Who

| Role | Does | Never |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lead | Decides what is flown, any override, any break of the freeze, when to roll back | Flies or types during a flight |
| Safety pilot | Holds the transmitter from arming to disarming; takes over at any doubt | Looks at a screen in flight |
| Operator | Types the commands, reads the preflight and the modes aloud | Sends a mode or a command during an autonomous flight: it costs the autonomy bonus |
| Spotter | Watches the aircraft and the flight area, calls positions and people | Looks away |

## Before the competition

1. The flight controller holds the 2027 baseline and the site's fence (`platform/fcu/README.md`).
2. The freeze is tagged and the 2026 fallback is built (`docs/ops/freeze_and_rollback.md`).
3. The readiness flight is flown, filmed and submitted (`docs/ops/readiness_video.md`).
4. The slot plan is chosen from the scoring model (`python3 tools/score_model.py`).

## At the field, once

1. The day file: `python3 tools/field_setup.py field/<day>.yaml --for-flight`. No coordinate is typed anywhere else.
2. The fence of the day is uploaded and read back.
3. The "Start of the day" checklist.

## Each flight

1. When the team is called: the operator starts the slot clock (`python3 tools/slot_clock.py start --slot <n>`). Its line is the time left in the slot and until the list is due; the GO command prints the same line before the preflight and at GO, and warns when less of the slot is left than a flight is budgeted. It stops nothing: flying late is the lead's call.
2. The "by hand" checklist.
3. The operator starts the flight with one command, which runs the preflight and starts nothing on NO-GO:

   ```bash
   python3 tools/go.py --profile <profile> --sequence field/<name>/sequences/<sequence>.yaml --params live_target_mission.yaml \
       --camera <topic>=<rate> --param-dump <today's dump> --clock-source <ground laptop> --record <log folder>/<attempt>
   ```

   The preflight's checks, in order: `params`, `fence`, `gps`, `ekf`, `rangefinder`, `cameras`, `engine`, `timesync`, `disk`, `battery`, `profile`. Each is a line of the checklist.
   A flight that uses a trained model adds `--engine <file>`: without it the `engine` check compares nothing.
4. On `GO` the aircraft arms and flies the sequence. From arming to disarming nobody touches the transmitter's sticks or the ground station: any input is found by the audit and loses the bonus.
5. The safety pilot takes over at any doubt. A takeover is never wrong.
6. After the landing: the "After each flight" checklist. The attempt's folder is the record.

## Between flights

- A tuned value may change (a config YAML); it is committed with `[tuning: <reason>]` before it is flown. Code does not change (`tools/freeze_check.py`).
- If a 2027 behaviour misbehaves: fly the profile `comp_2026` (every flag off). If the workspace itself is in doubt: `platform/jetson/fallback.sh launch <2026 launch file>`.
- A battery under the preflight's voltage is not flown.

## What the aircraft will do by itself

| What happens | The aircraft |
| --- | --- |
| Fence breached | returns to the takeoff point (RTL), or lands |
| Battery low | returns to the takeoff point (RTL) |
| Battery critical | lands where it is |
| Transmitter lost | returns to the takeoff point (RTL) |
| Ground station lost | returns to the takeoff point (RTL); not while a person is flying it in LOITER, ALT_HOLD, STABILIZE or another pilot mode |
| Position estimate lost (EKF) | lands where it is |

The full table, and what each person does: `emergency_procedures.md`.
